extracted.intended_audience: writers creating multiple-choice / text-based interactive fiction (ChoiceScript/Choice of Games authors)
extracted.subtask_description: A six-pass, chapter-by-chapter workflow for planning, writing, and implementing non-linear text games (choice-based interactive fiction), covering structure, prose, variables, and exporting/scripting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass 1 – Stub Text (No Color)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lay down the chapter structure using stub dialog and placeholders rather than finished prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stub dialog as placeholders to indicate who will say what, when, and what the player's options are. If branches depend on stats or conditions, indicate the stat and describe options in plain English. Do not write game logic yet. Avoid excessive revisions (or any) in this pass; its purpose is to get a high-level roadmap of the chapter. The output should be a first draft roadmap for subsequent passes (example: indicate Telepathy or Body Language checks without scripting them).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass 2 – Stub Text Revision (Yellow)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise only the structure established in Pass 1, fixing placement and flow of choices and branches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus exclusively on the placement of scenes/choices—do not worry about spelling or prose. Look for choices or branches that don't make sense, inconsistencies with the story, edge cases that could break flow, and dead ends that don't reconnect to the main narrative. Secondarily, ensure you are using the planned player stats/abilities in this chapter; if not, decide to amend the plan, add sequences that use them, or note to use them later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass 3 – First-Pass Text (Orange)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the actual in-game text the player will see based on the refined structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrate on pure writing—dialogue, descriptions, and the prose players read. Do not worry about setting variable values, scripting transitions, or other technical details during this pass. This is the most time-intensive and enjoyable pass; maintain focus to produce complete readable text for each node.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass 4 – Text Revision (Purple)
rubrics_metrics.description: Edit the prose aggressively to correct and tighten all text-related issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter editor mode: fix spelling, grammar, incorrect references to characters/places, choose tighter wording, and generally make the text sing. This pass targets anything related to the visible text rather than structure or variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass 5 – Variables (Blue)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and set up all instances where player stats, variables, and unique cases affect outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Go through the chapter looking specifically for variable use: where stats are referenced or modified to determine outcomes, and any special-case items or one-off encounters. Set baseline values for checks that can be refined later during playtesting and balancing. Keep an external reference document recording stat thresholds per chapter to maintain internal consistency across the game (example: if Strength 45 is required to kick a wooden door in Chapter 4, require ~65 for knocking down a metal door in Chapter 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass 6 – Export and Logic (Green)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring the (almost) finished chapter into your development environment and implement the game logic and formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Export or copy the chapter into your development tool (Chat Mapper exports XML/JSON/Excel/Rich Text; ChoiceScript requires copying/formatting). As you import, adjust formatting and segment transitions and begin scripting the underlying logic. Because structure and content are resolved, scripting becomes a problem-solving task divorced from creative writing. Optionally, you can export stub text earlier to play through; Chat Mapper supports Lua if you prefer scripting inside it, but be aware you may rescript in your final environment. Overall advice: tackle one task at a time, celebrate milestones, take notes for improvement, and prioritize playtesting and consistency.
